criteriaVerbatim:
PHASE A — FROZEN SECURITY / MAINTAINABILITY / PERFORMANCE QUALITY MATRIX

Disposition: criteria preparation complete. Implementation, integration evidence, experiments and delivery are NOT ASSESSED. The correctness field describes this Phase A deliverable, not the unseen candidate. Only the outcome-blind scope and relevant review, evidence-identity, security, architecture, performance, code-quality and test-quality references were read. Scope-document checkmarks were not accepted as execution evidence. No repository implementation, diff, prior review, gate output or paid result was inspected; no mutation or verification command was performed.

ASSESSMENT RULES

Each numbered criterion below freezes the contract, evidence needed and SHIP/FIX-FIRST/BLOCKED triggers. SHIP requires evidence of the stated invariant. FIX-FIRST requires a demonstrated, actionable contract violation or attributable failed required validation. BLOCKED means missing identity, evidence, authorization or environmental prerequisite prevents assessment or completion; it is not a finding of an implementation defect. Unsupported hypotheses are not confirmed findings. Nonblocking style preferences and bounded maintenance nits do not invalidate correctness. Findings in Phase B must identify the exact candidate, affected boundary, trigger, impact and evidence provenance. New criteria introduced after inspection must be explicitly labelled rather than retroactively presented as frozen requirements.

FROZEN THREAT MODEL

Trusted authority: explicit operator configuration and sanctioned credentials; the approved public engine controls; pinned SDK contracts; owning runtime validators; frozen source/fixture provenance; canonical native workflow and billing consumers. Model output, recursive tool arguments, repository text, filenames, symlinks, local Git configuration, ambient SDK resources, provider errors and externally returned catalog/viewer/JEV bodies are data, not authority. A repository under examination cannot grant broader filesystem, process, credential, Git or billing authority through instructions or configuration. A project key grants project-scoped inference/viewer access, not administrative exports. Bench and workflow observations describe events; they cannot manufacture identities, measured usage or verification success. Pi is explicitly read-only and isolated. RLM's approved Python execution must not be misrepresented as a general security sandbox; this review checks its specified lifecycle, scope and side-effect guarantees without inventing a new sandbox architecture.

NUMBERED QUALITY CRITERIA

Q01 — Exact content identity and evidence attribution.
Contract: Phase B assesses the complete G1–G9 candidate, not merely the latest patch. Bind a sorted bytes-and-mode manifest, algorithm, file count, digest and explicit exclusions; include untracked and generated artifacts. Relate that identity to candidate SHA, supplied validation and final remote head/base.
Evidence: immutable candidate inventory and attributable coordinator receipts, including identity after validation; full approved-scope-to-evidence map.
SHIP: reviewed bytes, validated bytes and delivered bytes agree, with no acceptance-critical artifact silently excluded. FIX-FIRST: demonstrated identity drift, excluded shipped content or misattributed receipts must be corrected and relevant reviews refreshed. BLOCKED: missing or ambiguous identity prevents assessment. A branch name or earlier verdict is insufficient.

Q02 — Source, original WIP and operator-state preservation.
Contract: retain the non-squash Mikro import at 62894e49314bad07382492ac074ea96df6776f61, exact initial subtree identity and independent npm authority; preserve original checkout HEAD/index/WIP, unrelated installer/CLI/CHANGELOG work and existing operator auth/settings.
Evidence: ancestry and initial-tree proof; attributable before/after HEAD/index, dirty-file and operator-state inventories; complete changed-path inventory.
SHIP: required import identities and preservation agree. FIX-FIRST: an actual unauthorized mutation or unrelated change is demonstrated. BLOCKED: absent baseline/provenance prevents establishing preservation. Current final files alone cannot prove original WIP was untouched.

Q03 — Package, retirement and standalone-update authority.
Contract: parent discovery exclusions isolate only independently gated Mikro; imported skills/history do not fall under Genie retirement authority. Nested standalone update is rejected before owner/journal/fetch/reset/clean mutation.
Evidence: discovery and update entry points through their consumers; real boundary regression receipts and standalone install/update proof.
SHIP: independent package authority holds without removing existing Genie coverage. FIX-FIRST: an exclusion hides unrelated tests, retirement consumes imported ownership, or a nested update reaches mutation before denial. BLOCKED: missing owning-boundary or installed proof leaves the authority contract unverified.

Q04 — Dependency and provider identity.
Contract: directly used Pi-family packages are exactly 1.0.2 under Mikro's npm lock and Node >=22.19.0; custom providers and operator auth/sampling/cache/output settings retain their behavior; built-in deepseek/deepseek-flash resolves without obsolete repository provider shadowing. No Prime re-pin or scored Prime arm.
Evidence: manifest/lock/import graph and dependency API/types; dependency-backed provider regressions; compiled generic query with repository configuration and no model override.
SHIP: identities, settings and actual resolution agree. FIX-FIRST: wrong package versions, duplicate incompatible provider identities, lost controls or shadowed defaults are demonstrated. BLOCKED: missing resolution or compiled-call evidence prevents claiming operational compatibility.

Q05 — Explicit credential and project boundaries.
Contract: Juice remains disabled until explicitly configured; assigned projects have distinct private keys, directory 0700/file 0600, credential references rather than public secrets. Provisioning is supported, additive/idempotent and does not alter unrelated keys. Invocation credentials never mutate global provider state across callers. Management authority is restricted to explicit provisioning, not ordinary inference/viewer calls.
Evidence: configuration-to-client credential flow; permission and secret-safe output receipts; provisioning before/after inventory; project-specific catalog/call receipts; overlapping-call isolation proof where global state could otherwise be shared.
SHIP: every credential use remains within its configured invocation/project/operation. FIX-FIRST: key crossover, ambient activation, public secret exposure, insecure storage or unrelated key modification is shown. BLOCKED: unavailable sanctioned provisioning/auth or missing isolation evidence prevents an operational claim.

Q06 — Secret-safe failures and external responses.
Contract: credentials, cookies and sensitive response bodies cannot leak through argv, logs, exceptions, manifests, source, commits or chat. Provider errors remain meaningful without exposing authentication material; malformed external bodies do not become success.
Evidence: success and transport/auth/body/schema-failure paths through CLI, MCP, provider and viewer/JEV consumers; redacted negative-case receipts with independent assertions that no secret escaped.
SHIP: safe failures retain truthful classification. FIX-FIRST: a traced path discloses a secret or masks an external failure as success. BLOCKED: absent failure-path evidence leaves that boundary unverified. Redaction must not erase the failure semantics needed for diagnosis.

Q07 — Filesystem scope and Pi ambient-resource isolation.
Contract: Pi exposes only scoped read/grep/glob/git/emit_done; realpath containment includes symlink escapes. Its ModelRuntime, SettingsManager, SessionManager and ResourceLoader do not import ambient credentials, instructions, plugins, shell tools or mutable resources. Recursive discovery and subsequent reads preserve the same authority boundary.
Evidence: entry-to-tool dispatch and tool-to-filesystem traces; actual SDK execution; adversarial absolute/traversal/symlink/out-of-root/ambient-resource tests at the real tool boundary, including recursive results and their later consumption.
SHIP: all reachable operations remain in the approved read-only scope. FIX-FIRST: any tool, resource loader or recursive path exposes unauthorized access or mutation. BLOCKED: mocked tool declarations without dependency-backed scope proof cannot establish containment.

Q08 — Hermetic Git inspection.
Contract: allowed Git inspection is read-only and cannot execute external diff/textconv/fsmonitor/pager/hooks or accept config-environment injection; repository-controlled arguments/config cannot turn it into a command or mutation channel.
Evidence: allowlist, argument/environment construction and process invocation; adversarial configured-repository receipts showing denial or inert behavior, rather than simply checking advertised capabilities.
SHIP: permitted inspection works while execution/mutation paths remain closed. FIX-FIRST: a specific allowed invocation can cross this boundary. BLOCKED: missing real Git/config boundary evidence prevents a security SHIP for this surface.

Q09 — Proposal versus evidence authority and frozen fixtures.
Contract: NEW is proposal-only in top-level plan.files, with missing path, no line, tracked nearest ancestor and containment checks. It cannot authorize ordinary citations, untracked/ignored existing files, traversal, escapes or evidence-dedup leakage. Added-file cases execute against frozen parent trees with implementations absent, preserving evaluation/source/parent provenance.
Evidence: verifier-to-score consumer traces; positive and independently targeted negative boundary tests; four fixture identities, parent-tree inventories and generator CLI proof.
SHIP: proposal/file/citation scoring stays distinct and leakage-free. FIX-FIRST: NEW grants citation authority, stale success survives failure, or a fixture contains the answer implementation. BLOCKED: unavailable frozen provenance or parent-tree proof invalidates the affected comparison.

Q10 — Provider termination and bounded retry accounting.
Contract: error/aborted/length are typed failures, never empty successful answers; reported usage survives failure once. Transport retry default is three and explicit zero is honored without adding other retry layers.
Evidence: provider-to-RLM/Pi/MCP/caller failure dispatch, owning regressions and actual provider-boundary receipts; attempt counts and usage ledger reconciliation.
SHIP: classifications, retries and charges remain truthful. FIX-FIRST: a new stop value is dropped by a consumer, a retry limit is ignored, or failure usage is lost/doubled. BLOCKED: missing actual boundary proof prevents the specified operational claim.

Q11 — RLM final protocol and budget integrity.
Contract: bare safe FINAL identifiers resolve variables; quoted values stay literal; arbitrary expressions are not evaluated; missing variables and ellipsis produce repair feedback. Final schema validation occurs inside iteration/token/cost/deadline limits, with no extra forced completion beyond the cap.
Evidence: parser-to-runtime-to-result consumer traces; identifier/quoted/missing/ellipsis regressions; actual model-call and final-validation receipts at boundary budgets.
SHIP: only valid final answers succeed and limits bound every completion. FIX-FIRST: expression execution, false success, ignored feedback or out-of-budget finalization is demonstrated. BLOCKED: unmeasured call counts or missing boundary-finalization proof prevent assessing the caps.

Q12 — Timeout, bridge and process lifecycle.
Contract: typed REPL timeout terminates/waits/detaches the old child, rejects stale bridge replies, restores approved context/tools with visible user-variable loss and never replays timed-out code. Restart/deadline failure is terminal. Pi cancellation/deadline/abort and disposal release sessions and processes without continuing tools after completion.
Evidence: actual Python side-effect-once and fresh-state receipts; stale-reply/restart-failure/deadline regressions; SDK abort/disposal boundary evidence and cross-backend signal handling.
SHIP: work stops and lifecycle transitions are explicit and bounded. FIX-FIRST: duplicate side effects, stale state contamination, surviving unauthorized work, hidden state loss or a dropped cancellation signal is shown. BLOCKED: mocks alone cannot establish real child/session containment.

Q13 — Public selector and unchanged defaults.
Contract: engine is rlm|pi|prime|prime-sdk; call > agent > rlm precedence is strict, including generic query. Unknown/empty/non-string engines and obsolete backend keys fail before billing. No shape heuristic, silent fallback, automatic routing, native-stage model change or operator-config migration. Wish omission preserves existing RLM behavior; off disables both scout and review offloads.
Evidence: configuration, MCP, backend registry, call/bench and both wish dispatch paths; compiled selector/error receipts and owning workflow behavior tests; complete old-selector caller inventory.
SHIP: selected treatments reach both consumers and off/default behavior is unchanged. FIX-FIRST: a selector is decorative/dropped, a fallback changes treatment, stale aliases remain active or rejection follows billing. BLOCKED: missing real caller/compiled dispatch proof prevents an end-to-end feature claim.

Q14 — Pi finalization and outward compatibility.
Contract: Pi is protocol-free, uses the supported SDK tool loop, validates tool and final schemas with declared precedence, accepts the first valid final and stops after that turn. Missing/invalid final is a meaningful failure, not a last-paragraph fallback. MCP structuredContent {answer, session_id}, priced footer, history, progress heartbeat and failure classification remain compatible.
Evidence: SDK event/tool/final dispatch through RuntimeBackend, MCP, ledger/history and Genie consumers; actual valid/invalid/missing/schema-final and final-then-tool receipts; compiled envelopes and progress/history records.
SHIP: accepted finals and failures reach every owning consumer without extra work or envelope drift. FIX-FIRST: new events silently disappear, multiple finals overwrite success, post-final work continues or accounting/result contracts break. BLOCKED: dependency-backed loop or actual outward-surface evidence is missing.

Q15 — Viewer-only aggregate extraction.
Contract: manual usage/analyze authenticates with the project key, keeps viewer cookies in memory and uses only key-overview/key-analysis/key-analysis/latency aggregates. Snapshots preserve URL/query/project/key epoch/returned range/timezone/fetch time/hash and capabilities; unavailable costs/time fields remain unknown. No admin escalation, request/conversation export, invented request IDs or aggregate rebilling.
Evidence: authorization-to-route-to-snapshot-to-report traces; actual viewer/version/logout/project-scope receipts; unknown-field and secret-safe failure tests.
SHIP: snapshots are source-linked, project-scoped observations with honest limitations. FIX-FIRST: broader authority, cross-project data, fabricated detail or conversion of unknown to zero is demonstrated. BLOCKED: unavailable authorized viewer access or missing provenance blocks actual snapshot completion.

Q16 — One-shot manual JEV selection.
Contract: one explicit configured endpoint/model/key request follows {state,model,questions}; Choice supports bounded candidate IDs and abstention, optional Noul/Score stay in that request, response/model/probabilities/usage are validated and source links are locally reattached. Cancellation works. No retries, translation, caching, generation, routing, schedules or source mutation; ordinary runs invoke neither JEV nor extra instrumentation inference.
Evidence: manual caller-to-adapter-to-result traces; typed malformed/abstention/source-mapping tests; real sanctioned manual extraction receipt; ordinary-run network/call evidence; preserved snapshot hashes and candidate source spans.
SHIP: exactly the requested manual selection occurs with typed observed usage and source fidelity. FIX-FIRST: automatic invocation, extra call, fabricated fallback, invalid success or wrong source mapping is shown. BLOCKED: an unavailable sanctioned endpoint/auth blocks live extraction, not reachable adapter review; expired AWS SSO is not permission to substitute an unsanctioned public service.

Q17 — Maintainability and six-month change cost.
Contract: reuse RuntimeBackend, supported SDK loop, verifier/ledger/report consumers and saved wish runner; keep npm/Node and Bun/release domains intentionally independent. Remove obsolete selectors/callers/shims and temporary scaffolds, update affected docs/changelogs, and keep experiment observation local rather than introducing a second accounting or workflow system. Runtime-validated boundary types should not become unchecked interior type holes.
Evidence: complete import/interface/caller graph and ownership map; state-machine/error paths; affected docs; attributable full quality gates and existing policy/baselines.
SHIP: each added mechanism serves an approved current requirement and interfaces have one clear authority. FIX-FIRST: demonstrated contract-breaking state machinery, consumer duplication, dead compatibility paths or type holes with concrete failure impact. BLOCKED: an architectural scope decision is missing or repairing unjustified machinery would change the approved approach. Stylistic extraction, deliberate package separation and unsupported complexity preferences are not blocking findings.

Q18 — Concrete allocation, computation and resource bounds.
Contract: review actual hot paths for repeated full-tree scans, avoidable copies/serialization, eager unrelated SDK/resource loading, repeated catalog/config work, unbounded tool output/history and recursive calls that evade declared limits. Preserve required validation, provenance and correctness retries; no speculative cache/daemon/compaction or new tuning API.
Evidence: exact shipped-path call sites, repetition/input bounds and attributable resource/latency measurements; cold-start versus repeated-run results where relevant; full computation and model/tool call counts, including failed attempts.
SHIP: resource work is bounded and no concrete introduced overhead violates required budgets or measured non-regression. FIX-FIRST: a traced repeated allocation/computation or runaway recursion causes a demonstrated cap, latency, memory or compatibility failure. BLOCKED: missing measurements prevent a performance claim, not a speculative code defect. Minor bounded overhead is not automatically a blocker.

Q19 — Behavioral test ownership and complete gates.
Contract: tests protect observable boundaries with independent oracles and credible regressions, not copied defaults/source text or mocks that supply the behavior. Isolation protects original repos, credentials and operator state. Real dependency/process/Git/provider/compiled/install boundaries receive the proof their contracts require; no test-only production seam or narrowed replacement for full gates.
Evidence: full owning tests and their production dispatch paths; pre-fix failure/post-fix receipts for repaired regressions; suite pass/fail/skip counts and exit codes; exact-candidate Mikro deps:ci/build/check/test/install-update and Genie frozen install/check receipts plus actual CLI/MCP/release checks.
SHIP: required full gates and boundary proof pass for the candidate. FIX-FIRST: attributable required gate failure, a security/accounting test passing for the wrong guard, or a high-impact accepted behavior not actually exercised. BLOCKED: absent/stale/skipped required validation prevents SHIP. The reviewer consumes coordinator evidence and performs no builds, mutation probes or resampling.

Q20 — Exact matched experiments and honest selection.
Contract: retain all four frozen Genie/brain existing/new-directory fixtures, three reps per Flash control arm, all 36 control runs; freeze and separately execute/report each available curated candidate cell. Freeze launcher/runtime/artifact/schema/prompt/pricing/catalog identities before outcomes; concurrency is one. Retain every failure, retry and unknown. No Pro/Claude calls, scored Prime arm or post-outcome resampling.
Evidence: immutable manifests, catalog exclusions and all attempt receipts; paired cell metrics for file/NEW/citation verification, all-attempt and run p50/p90 latency, cost per verified success, cost coverage, cap share and repetition dispersion.
SHIP: planned cells and attempts are complete and any recommendation satisfies cell-wise verified-success parity plus real-workflow non-regression. FIX-FIRST: omitted failures, treatment mismatch, leakage, unsupported speed/cost claim or success-parity violation. BLOCKED: missing cells, pricing/usage coverage or provenance prevents comparison SHIP. Aggregate speed cannot compensate for a failing repository/model cell, and equal failure rates do not establish useful verified success.

Q21 — Genuine wish outcomes and canonical business/adoption accounting.
Contract: execute two bounded objectives × three treatments × three reps as 18 actual saved-wish runs in isolated repository/common-directory/state roots. First prove the native loader, non-Claude route and observer in an unscored actual smoke. Retain real workflow UUID/seq/childId, outcomes/SHIP/repairs, stage tokens/tools/durations/offloads and runtime failures. Count persisted own-suffix native assistant/message and assistant/attempt usage once, tool/call events once, and lifecycle durations from actual events; reconcile inherited/forked usage, failed attempts, priced offloads and aggregate Keeper spend without double billing. Append existing reports only when all required top-level accounting is measured and compatible; never redesign frozen consumers, invent IDs/totals/zero usage or equate a success journal with accounting.
Evidence: native session/event persistence and observer dispatch; 18 treatment/outcome receipts; stage-to-run reconciliation and report consumer/schema acceptance; explicit coverage/unknown ledger and separate aggregate snapshots.
SHIP: all runs and required accounting are real, complete and compatible; business/adoption recommendations reflect verified outcomes, cost per verified success, repair burden and coverage rather than token price or latency alone. FIX-FIRST: incorrect deduplication, invented receipts, unknown-as-zero, false report append or a surrogate pipeline is demonstrated. BLOCKED: any missing required usage/stage identity/cost field blocks completed accounting comparison even if all outcomes are successful. Honest incomplete records may be retained, but cannot be called a completed comparison.

Q22 — Installed artifacts, release payload and remote delivery.
Contract: compiled Mikro dist/install/CLI/MCP behavior matches reviewed source and exact dependency family; Genie binary/tarball payload and runtime dependency boundary remain unchanged. Independent execution and quality review cover the candidate. Deliver a committed exact-path merge-ready PR to Genie dev with current remote head/base/files/CI readback. No main promotion, merge, production installation/update or source deletion; wish remains IN_PROGRESS until authorized merge/QA.
Evidence: source-to-dist and installed-path receipts; original-versus-candidate release inventory and runtime dependency proof; full gates/reviews tied to candidate identity; live target/head/file/CI and merge-readiness evidence supplied by the coordinator.
SHIP: installed/release behavior, source preservation, reviews and current remote checks agree. FIX-FIRST: generated/installed drift, Mikro leakage into Genie payload, wrong target, stale review presented as current or unauthorized mutation is demonstrated. BLOCKED: missing installed/release proof, live remote readback or current required CI prevents whole-delivery SHIP. Local green alone does not establish remote readiness.

FROZEN VERDICT COMPOSITION AND G8/G9 RECONCILIATION

1. Source-quality SHIP: no confirmed blocking security, correctness, maintainability or resource defect in the exact reviewed source/artifact scope, with its required attributable validation. State separately any unavailable live integration; source-quality SHIP cannot be represented as proof that an unexercised feature works operationally. Feature/runtime SHIP additionally requires the named applicable actual provider/REPL/Pi/MCP/caller/Juice/JEV/installed surfaces.

2. Comparison SHIP: Q20 and Q21 are fully satisfied, including every exact experiment and complete canonical accounting. A performance or adoption recommendation additionally requires cell-wise verified-success parity and no real workflow SHIP/repair regression. An accurately reported non-advantage is acceptable; the obligation is honest comparison, not selecting Pi or claiming a win.

3. Whole-delivery SHIP: every G1–G9 obligation, source/runtime/comparison reviews, original-state protection, full gates, installed/release behavior and current merge-ready dev PR evidence is satisfied. No source verdict alone closes the wish, authorizes publication or substitutes for another independent review.

4. G9's exercised-proof-or-exact-unreachable-prerequisite clause permits an honest explicit blocker disposition, not acceptance by omission. An unreachable prerequisite must identify the precise sanctioned endpoint/auth/capability/data/environment needed, the authorized discovery/access paths already tried, their attributable failure and exactly which criteria remain incomplete. Missing evidence is not automatically proof that a prerequisite is unreachable. Finish all reachable review work; do not substitute fake output, forbidden admin access, public inference or paid reruns.

5. G8's missing-accounting rule remains binding even when the exact prerequisite is unreachable. Thus source-quality may independently SHIP, while runtime/comparison/whole-delivery remain BLOCKED where appropriate; no fully measured report append or completed-comparison claim is allowed. An exact blocker satisfies truthful reporting, not the missing experiment/accounting acceptance criterion. Scope may change only through explicit owner authorization, not reviewer reinterpretation.

6. A confirmed actionable blocker produces FIX-FIRST for the affected verdict. A missing assessment/completion prerequisite produces BLOCKED for that affected verdict; confirmed defects must still be retained rather than hidden by the blocker. Phase B must report the separate source-quality, feature/runtime, comparison and whole-delivery dispositions and coverage. Relevant source, generated-content, dependency, fixture or evidence changes invalidate affected reviews and receipts; bounded author repairs do not silently relax this frozen matrix.

PHASE B HANDOFF

Required inputs are the exact candidate identity and full approved diff/context; attributable preservation, complete gate and actual-surface receipts; frozen experiment manifests and all retained attempts; native workflow/session/accounting reconciliation; installed/release evidence; and current remote dev-PR identity/checks. This reviewer remains independent and read-only. No source edits, git-state changes, provisioning, model/JEV requests, tests, formatters or resampling are authorized.
